lesson_title: Double Entry and the Accounting Equation
hook_text: One equation runs every business on Earth. A = O + L. Here's why it can never break.
clip_script: Let us begin with a statement so simple it looks almost too obvious: everything a business owns was funded by somebody. Either the owner supplied the money, or someone outside the business did. What the business owns, we call assets. What the owner supplied, we call owner's equity. What outsiders supplied, we call liabilities. Because every asset was funded from one of those two sources, we can write the accounting equation: A equals O plus L. This is not a rule someone invented to torment learners — it is a statement of fact, true at every moment of a business's life. If it ever stops balancing, the books contain an error. Full stop.
visual_style: Bold three-panel scale animation: assets on one pan, equity plus liabilities on the other, staying level as transactions drop in.
pacing: Slow, weighty opening line, then accelerating as the equation assembles.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and balance all four transactions yourself.
